subtitle: "The Flowchart"

The chart below gives a rough layout of the finite element method in one dimension.
This integrates much of what you have learned previously and grounds the multidimensional in a case study.

Switch between **hard-coded assembly** and **general polynomial degree** and note the similarities and the differences. 
This is a clean representation of how to use the basis functions and quadrature points to operate within a 1D finite element code that has been hard-coded to work with linear hat functions.

```{=html}
<style>
.fc15{--ink:#18202b;--grey:#6b7684;--faint:#dfe4ea;--paper:#f8f9fb;
      --acc:#b8322a;--amb:#e0a800;--ambbg:#fff6da;
      max-width:900px;margin:0 auto;color:var(--ink)}
.fc15 .bar{display:flex;flex-wrap:wrap;gap:10px 18px;align-items:center;
  padding:11px 14px;background:var(--paper);border:1px solid var(--faint);
  border-radius:8px;margin-bottom:14px}
.fc15 .bar b{font-size:12.5px;letter-spacing:.05em;color:var(--grey)}
.fc15 .seg{display:inline-flex;border:1px solid var(--faint);border-radius:6px;
  overflow:hidden;background:#fff}
.fc15 .seg button{border:0;background:#fff;padding:6px 14px;font:inherit;font-size:14px;
  cursor:pointer;color:var(--grey);border-right:1px solid var(--faint)}
.fc15 .seg button:last-child{border-right:0}
.fc15 .seg button[aria-pressed="true"]{background:var(--ink);color:#fff}
.fc15 .seg button:disabled{opacity:.35;cursor:default}

  border:1px solid var(--faint);border-radius:8px;background:#fff}
.fc15 .cap{font-size:13px;color:var(--grey);line-height:1.55;margin:9px 2px 0}
.fc15 .cap b{color:var(--ink)}
</style>

<div class="fc15">
  <div class="bar">
    <b>VERSION</b>
    <span class="seg" id="fcver">
      <button data-v="p1" aria-pressed="true">Hard-coded&nbsp;assembly</button>
      <button data-v="c15" aria-pressed="false">General&nbsp;polynomial&nbsp;degree</button>
    </span>
    <b>DEGREE</b>
    <span class="seg" id="fcdeg">
      <button data-p="1" aria-pressed="true">p&nbsp;=&nbsp;1</button>
      <button data-p="2" aria-pressed="false">p&nbsp;=&nbsp;2</button>
      <button data-p="3" aria-pressed="false">p&nbsp;=&nbsp;3</button>
    </span>
  </div>
  <svg id="fcsvg" viewBox="0 0 880 1210" role="img"
       aria-label="Flowchart of the finite element solver"></svg>
  <div class="cap" id="fccap"></div>
</div>

<script>
(function(){
var V='p1', P=1;
var INK='#18202b', GREY='#6b7684', FAINT='#dfe4ea', ACC='#b8322a',
    PAPER='#f8f9fb', AMB='#ffe9a8', S='';

function esc(t){return String(t).replace(/&/g,'&amp;').replace(/</g,'&lt;');}
function box(x,y,w,h,fill,stroke,sw){
  S+='<rect x="'+x+'" y="'+y+'" width="'+w+'" height="'+h+'" rx="7" fill="'+(fill||'#fff')+
     '" stroke="'+(stroke||INK)+'" stroke-width="'+(sw||1.3)+'"/>';}
function txt(x,y,t,o){o=o||{};
  S+='<text x="'+x+'" y="'+y+'" font-size="'+(o.s||13)+'" fill="'+(o.f||INK)+
     '" text-anchor="'+(o.a||'start')+'" font-weight="'+(o.w||400)+
     '" font-family="'+(o.m?'ui-monospace,Menlo,monospace':'inherit')+
     '" letter-spacing="'+(o.ls||0)+'">'+esc(t)+'</text>';}
function arrow(x,y1,y2,col){col=col||INK;
  S+='<line x1="'+x+'" y1="'+y1+'" x2="'+x+'" y2="'+(y2-7)+'" stroke="'+col+'" stroke-width="1.5"/>';
  S+='<path d="M'+(x-4.5)+' '+(y2-7)+' L'+x+' '+y2+' L'+(x+4.5)+' '+(y2-7)+'Z" fill="'+col+'"/>';}
function dot(x,y,r,f){S+='<circle cx="'+x+'" cy="'+y+'" r="'+r+'" fill="'+f+'"/>';}
function ring(x,y,r,f){S+='<circle cx="'+x+'" cy="'+y+'" r="'+r+'" fill="#fff" stroke="'+f+'" stroke-width="2"/>';}
function grid(x,y,n,c,fill){ // n x n cells of size c
  for(var i=0;i<n;i++)for(var j=0;j<n;j++)
    S+='<rect x="'+(x+j*c)+'" y="'+(y+i*c)+'" width="'+c+'" height="'+c+
       '" fill="'+(fill||'none')+'" stroke="'+GREY+'" stroke-width=".8"/>';}
function vec(x,y,n,c,fill){
  for(var i=0;i<n;i++)
    S+='<rect x="'+x+'" y="'+(y+i*c)+'" width="'+c+'" height="'+c+
       '" fill="'+(fill||'none')+'" stroke="'+GREY+'" stroke-width=".8"/>';}

/* ---------- pictograms, drawn in a 92 x 56 cell at (ox, oy) ---------- */
function picMesh(ox,oy){
  var x0=ox+4,x1=ox+88,y=oy+28,nb=3*P+1;
  S+='<line x1="'+x0+'" y1="'+y+'" x2="'+x1+'" y2="'+y+'" stroke="'+INK+'" stroke-width="1.4"/>';
  for(var e=0;e<=3;e++){var xx=x0+(x1-x0)*e/3;
    S+='<line x1="'+xx+'" y1="'+(y-7)+'" x2="'+xx+'" y2="'+(y+7)+'" stroke="'+INK+'" stroke-width="1.4"/>';}
  for(var A=0;A<nb;A++) dot(x0+(x1-x0)*A/(nb-1),y,2.8,(A%P===0)?INK:ACC);
}
function picID(ox,oy){
  var x0=ox+4,x1=ox+88,y=oy+28,nb=3*P+1;
  S+='<line x1="'+x0+'" y1="'+y+'" x2="'+x1+'" y2="'+y+'" stroke="'+FAINT+'" stroke-width="1.4"/>';
  for(var A=0;A<nb;A++){var xx=x0+(x1-x0)*A/(nb-1);
    if(A===nb-1) ring(xx,y,3.6,ACC); else dot(xx,y,3,INK);}
  txt(ox+46,oy+50,'unknown / given',{s:8.5,a:'middle',f:GREY});
}
function picEmpty(ox,oy){
  var n=Math.min(3*P,6), c=Math.min(9,34/n);
  grid(ox+6,oy+13,n,c,'#fff'); vec(ox+6+n*c+9,oy+13,n,c,'#fff');
}
function picElem(ox,oy){
  var x0=ox+14,x1=ox+78,y=oy+28;
  S+='<rect x="'+(x0-6)+'" y="'+(y-12)+'" width="'+(x1-x0+12)+'" height="24" rx="4" fill="'+AMB+'" opacity=".55"/>';
  S+='<line x1="'+x0+'" y1="'+y+'" x2="'+x1+'" y2="'+y+'" stroke="'+INK+'" stroke-width="1.4"/>';
  for(var a=0;a<=P;a++) dot(x0+(x1-x0)*a/P,y,3.2,INK);
}
function picQuadPt(ox,oy){
  var x0=ox+12,x1=ox+80,y=oy+40,nq=P+1;
  S+='<line x1="'+x0+'" y1="'+y+'" x2="'+x1+'" y2="'+y+'" stroke="'+INK+'" stroke-width="1.3"/>';
  for(var q=0;q<nq;q++){var xx=x0+(x1-x0)*(q+0.5)/nq;
    S+='<path d="M'+(xx-3.4)+' '+(y-3.4)+' L'+(xx+3.4)+' '+(y+3.4)+' M'+(xx+3.4)+' '+(y-3.4)+
       ' L'+(xx-3.4)+' '+(y+3.4)+'" stroke="'+ACC+'" stroke-width="1.6"/>';
    S+='<line x1="'+xx+'" y1="'+(y-7)+'" x2="'+xx+'" y2="'+(oy+16)+'" stroke="'+ACC+
       '" stroke-width=".9" stroke-dasharray="2 2"/>';}
  grid(ox+34,oy+4,2,6,'#fff');
}
function picKeFe(ox,oy,closed){
  var n=P+1,c=Math.min(13,40/n),gx=ox+10,gy=oy+28-n*c/2;
  grid(gx,gy,n,c,closed?PAPER:'#fff');
  if(closed){ // the +/- checkerboard of the Hughes form
    for(var i=0;i<2;i++)for(var j=0;j<2;j++)
      txt(gx+j*c+c/2,gy+i*c+c/2+3.5,(i===j)?'+':'−',{s:9,a:'middle',f:GREY});
  } else {
    for(var i2=0;i2<n;i2++)for(var j2=0;j2<n;j2++)
      S+='<rect x="'+(gx+j2*c+1.5)+'" y="'+(gy+i2*c+1.5)+'" width="'+(c-3)+'" height="'+(c-3)+
         '" fill="'+ACC+'" opacity="'+(0.13+0.1*((i2+j2)%3))+'"/>';
  }
  vec(gx+n*c+10,gy,n,c,closed?PAPER:'#fff');
}
function picScatter(ox,oy){
  var n=Math.min(3*P,6),c=Math.min(9,34/n);
  grid(ox+40,oy+13,n,c,'#fff');
  var m=Math.min(P+1,3),cc=7;
  grid(ox+4,oy+20,m,cc,AMB);
  S+='<path d="M'+(ox+6+m*cc)+' '+(oy+24)+' q 12 -4 '+(34-m*cc)+' 0" stroke="'+ACC+
     '" stroke-width="1.2" fill="none" marker-end="url(#fcar)"/>';
}
function picSolve(ox,oy){
  var n=4,c=8,gy=oy+12;
  grid(ox+2,gy,n,c,PAPER); vec(ox+2+n*c+4,gy,n,c,'#fff');
  txt(ox+2+n*c+4+c+5,gy+n*c/2+4,'=',{s:12,f:GREY});
  vec(ox+2+n*c+4+c+14,gy,n,c,PAPER);
}
function picRebuild(ox,oy){
  var nb=3*P+1,c=Math.min(9,46/nb),x=ox+46-nb*c/2;
  for(var A=0;A<nb;A++)
    S+='<rect x="'+x+'" y="'+(oy+14+A*0)+'" width="'+c+'" height="'+c+
       '" fill="'+(A===nb-1?AMB:'#fff')+'" stroke="'+GREY+'" stroke-width=".8" '+
       'transform="translate('+(A*c)+',0)"/>';
  txt(ox+46,oy+40,'all '+nb+' coefficients',{s:8.5,a:'middle',f:GREY});
}
function picPlot(ox,oy){
  var x0=ox+8,x1=ox+84,yb=oy+46,h=30;
  S+='<line x1="'+x0+'" y1="'+yb+'" x2="'+x1+'" y2="'+yb+'" stroke="'+FAINT+'" stroke-width="1"/>';
  var u=function(t){return Math.sin(Math.PI*t)*0.95;}, d='', nb=3*P+1;
  if(P===1){ for(var A=0;A<nb;A++){var t=A/(nb-1);
      d+=(A?' L':'M')+(x0+(x1-x0)*t)+' '+(yb-h*u(t));} }
  else { for(var k=0;k<=36;k++){var t2=k/36;
      d+=(k?' L':'M')+(x0+(x1-x0)*t2)+' '+(yb-h*u(t2));} }
  S+='<path d="'+d+'" stroke="'+ACC+'" stroke-width="1.8" fill="none"/>';
  for(var A2=0;A2<nb;A2++){var t3=A2/(nb-1); dot(x0+(x1-x0)*t3,yb-h*u(t3),2.3,INK);}
}

/* ---------- layout ---------- */
function node(y,h,title,sub,pic,opt){
  opt=opt||{};
  var x=opt.x!==undefined?opt.x:210, w=opt.w!==undefined?opt.w:470;
  box(x,y,w,h,opt.fill||'#fff',opt.stroke||INK,opt.sw||1.3);
  pic(x+12,y+(h-56)/2);
  txt(x+118,y+(sub?h/2-4:h/2+5),title,{w:600,s:opt.ts||14.5});
  if(sub) txt(x+118,y+h/2+14,sub,{s:12.5,f:GREY});
  if(opt.badge){
    var bw=opt.badge.length*6.0+14;
    S+='<rect x="'+(x+w-bw-10)+'" y="'+(y+9)+'" width="'+bw+'" height="16" rx="3" fill="'+
       (opt.badgeFill||'#fbeeec')+'" stroke="'+(opt.badgeStroke||'#f0d4d0')+'"/>';
    txt(x+w-bw/2-10,y+20.5,opt.badge,{s:9.5,a:'middle',f:opt.badgeInk||ACC,w:700,ls:.5});
  }
  return y+h;
}
function loopFrame(x,y,w,h,label,col){
  col=col||GREY;
  S+='<rect x="'+x+'" y="'+y+'" width="'+w+'" height="'+h+'" rx="9" fill="none" stroke="'+col+
     '" stroke-width="1.2" stroke-dasharray="6 4"/>';
  var lw=label.length*7.0+20;
  S+='<rect x="'+(x+26)+'" y="'+(y-9)+'" width="'+lw+'" height="18" rx="4" fill="#fff" stroke="'+col+'" stroke-width="1"/>';
  txt(x+26+lw/2,y+3.5,label,{s:10.5,a:'middle',f:col,w:700,ls:.6});
  // a clean return line down the right margin, so the frame reads as a loop
  var rx=x+w-16, ty=y+16, by=y+h-16, r=9;
  S+='<path d="M'+(x+w-40)+' '+by+' H'+(rx-r)+' Q'+rx+' '+by+' '+rx+' '+(by-r)+
     ' V'+(ty+r)+' Q'+rx+' '+ty+' '+(rx-r)+' '+ty+' H'+(x+w-40)+
     '" stroke="'+col+'" stroke-width="1.2" fill="none" stroke-dasharray="4 3"'+
     ' marker-end="url(#'+(col===ACC?'fcar':'fcarg')+')"/>';
}

function draw(){
  S='<defs>'
   +'<marker id="fcar" markerWidth="7" markerHeight="7" refX="6" refY="3.5" orient="auto">'
   +'<path d="M0 0 L7 3.5 L0 7Z" fill="'+ACC+'"/></marker>'
   +'<marker id="fcarg" markerWidth="7" markerHeight="7" refX="6" refY="3.5" orient="auto">'
   +'<path d="M0 0 L7 3.5 L0 7Z" fill="'+GREY+'"/></marker></defs>';

  var c15=(V==='c15'), y=26, cx=445, GAP=26;

  txt(445,16,c15?('GENERAL POLYNOMIAL DEGREE  \u2014  here p = '+P)
                 :'HARD-CODED ASSEMBLY  \u2014  degree 1 only',
      {a:'middle',s:11.5,w:700,ls:1.4,f:c15?ACC:GREY});

  y=node(y,72,'The mesh and the data',
           'where the elements are, and where the basis functions sit', picMesh,
           c15?{badge:'n_bf = '+(3*P+1),badgeFill:'#fbeeec'}:{badge:'n_bf = 4',badgeFill:'#f1f3f6',badgeStroke:FAINT,badgeInk:GREY});
  arrow(cx,y,y+GAP); y+=GAP;

  y=node(y,72,'Decide what is unknown',
           'prescribed values get no equation — the ID array', picID);
  arrow(cx,y,y+GAP); y+=GAP;

  y=node(y,72,'Make room for the big system',
           'an empty K and F, one row per unknown', picEmpty);
  arrow(cx,y,y+GAP); y+=GAP;

  /* ------- the element loop ------- */
  var loopTop=y, inner=y+30;

  inner=node(inner,72,'Look at one element',
           'just its own nodes, mapped to the parent element', picElem,{x:232,w:426});
  arrow(cx,inner,inner+GAP); inner+=GAP;

  if(c15){
    var qTop=inner;
    var qi=node(inner+30,78,'Add one quadrature point’s contribution',
           'N, dN/d\u03be and J, evaluated right there', picQuadPt,
           {x:240,w:412,ts:13.5,fill:'#fffaf2',stroke:ACC,sw:1.4});
    loopFrame(226,qTop,440,qi-qTop+16,'FOR EACH QUADRATURE POINT',ACC);
    inner=qi+16;
    arrow(cx,inner,inner+GAP); inner+=GAP;
    inner=node(inner,72,'The element’s own matrix and vector',
           'built up point by point — size '+(P+1)+'×'+(P+1),
           function(a,b){picKeFe(a,b,false);},{x:232,w:426});
  } else {
    inner=node(inner,72,'The element’s own matrix and vector',
           'one formula, integrated by hand once, forever 2×2',
           function(a,b){picKeFe(a,b,true);},{x:232,w:426,
           badge:'CLOSED FORM',badgeFill:'#f1f3f6',badgeStroke:FAINT,badgeInk:GREY});
  }
  arrow(cx,inner,inner+GAP); inner+=GAP;

  inner=node(inner,72,'Add it into the big system',
           'IEN gives the global basis function, ID gives its equation',
           picScatter,{x:232,w:426,ts:14});

  loopFrame(216,loopTop,458,inner-loopTop+22,'FOR EACH ELEMENT',GREY);
  y=inner+22;
  arrow(cx,y,y+GAP); y+=GAP;

  y=node(y,72,'Solve','one linear system, K D = F', picSolve);
  arrow(cx,y,y+GAP); y+=GAP;

  y=node(y,72,'Put the prescribed values back',
           'so every basis function has a coefficient', picRebuild);
  arrow(cx,y,y+GAP); y+=GAP;

  y=node(y,76,'Evaluate and draw it',
           c15?'the solution between the nodes, not just at them'
              :'straight lines between the nodal values', picPlot,
           {});

  document.getElementById('fcsvg').setAttribute('viewBox','0 0 880 '+(y+26));
  document.getElementById('fcsvg').innerHTML=S;

  document.getElementById('fccap').innerHTML =
      'A flowchart of a hard-coded assembly is represented against one that allows for computation with general polynomial degree.';
}

document.getElementById('fcver').addEventListener('click',function(ev){
  var b=ev.target.closest('button'); if(!b) return; V=b.dataset.v;
  [].forEach.call(this.querySelectorAll('button'),function(x){
    x.setAttribute('aria-pressed',x===b?'true':'false');});
  var dg=document.getElementById('fcdeg');
  [].forEach.call(dg.querySelectorAll('button'),function(x){ x.disabled=(V!=='c15'); });
  if(V!=='c15'){ P=1;
    [].forEach.call(dg.querySelectorAll('button'),function(x){
      x.setAttribute('aria-pressed',x.dataset.p==='1'?'true':'false');});}
  draw();
});
document.getElementById('fcdeg').addEventListener('click',function(ev){
  var b=ev.target.closest('button'); if(!b||b.disabled) return; P=+b.dataset.p;
  [].forEach.call(this.querySelectorAll('button'),function(x){
    x.setAttribute('aria-pressed',x===b?'true':'false');});
  draw();
});
[].forEach.call(document.querySelectorAll('#fcdeg button'),function(x){x.disabled=true;});
draw();
})();
</script>
```

<!-- 
## What the picture is telling you

**The chart has the same shape in both versions.** Set up, loop over elements, build two
small arrays, add them into the big ones, solve, fill the prescribed values back in, draw
the answer. That sequence is not a degree-1 thing or a one-dimensional thing. It is what a
production code does in three dimensions with a million elements.

**Only one box changes.** With a single hard-coded degree, the element's matrix and vector
come out of a formula that was integrated once, by hand, and then written into the code.
That is possible because at degree 1 an element carries two basis functions and the Jacobian
$dx/d\xi = h^e/2$ is constant, so it leaves the integral. Neither of those survives at
$p \geq 2$, so the formula is replaced by the thing it was standing in for: a sum over
quadrature points.

**That is why a loop appears.** Nothing was reorganised to make room for it — the box that
said "use the formula" became a box that says "add up contributions", and adding up
contributions is a loop.

**Two arrays are needed to place a contribution, not one.** IEN answers *which global basis
function is local function $a$ of element $e$?* The ID array answers *does that basis
function have an equation, and which one?* Composed, $\mathrm{LM}(a,e) = \mathrm{ID}(\mathrm{IEN}(a,e))$,
they turn a local index pair into a row and column of the global system — or into $-1$, meaning
the value there is prescribed and its contribution moves to the right-hand side instead.

**The last box has to change too.** Drawing straight lines between nodal values is replaced by
evaluating $u^h(\xi) = \sum_a d_{\mathrm{IEN}(a,e)} N_a(\xi)$ inside each element. At degree 1
the straight lines happened to *be* the answer; at higher degree they are a different,
plausible-looking curve. Switch the degree control and watch the drawn solution stop passing
straight between its dots.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
